frames.narration: Account A holds 100 and account B holds 50. The rule that must always hold: the total is 150.
The application starts a transaction to move 100 from A to B.
Step one: debit A. The change is held pending inside the transaction; other users do not see it yet.
COMMIT. Both changes become visible together (atomicity), the invariant still holds (consistency), and the change is written to the log on disk (durability).
Now a transfer that goes wrong. The transaction debits account B, then the server crashes before the credit happens.
On restart the database sees an unfinished transaction and rolls it back. Without transactions the 100 would simply have vanished.
